text:
Previously, Li Ru advised Dong Zhuo to promote famous scholars to gain public prestige. Most officials followed this path, and thus he recommended the talent of Cai Yong. Zhuo ordered his summons, but Yong initially did not intend to go. Zhuo, enraged, sent a messenger to tell Yong: "If you do not come, I will exterminate your entire clan." Yong was terrified and had no choice but to obey the order and arrive. Zhuo was greatly pleased to see Yong and promoted his rank three times within a single month, appointing him as <term>Shizhong</term> <gloss>Palace Attendant</gloss>. He was treated with great intimacy and favor. <gloss>Just as Yang Xiong relied on Wang Feng, Yong was fated to be consumed like firewood from Mount Kunshan.</gloss>

Meanwhile, the Former Emperor <note>Shao Di, Liu Bian</note>, Empress Dowager He, and Consort Tang were imprisoned in the Everlasting Peace Palace. Their clothing and food supplies gradually dwindled. The Former Emperor’s tears never dried. <gloss>This mirrors what a later king said: "The days and months in this place are unbearable."</gloss> One day, he happened to see a pair of swallows flying in the courtyard and composed a poem. <gloss>In the empty courtyard, birds soar and dance; in the cold, abandoned palace, he is solitary and aged before his time.</gloss> The poem read:

The tender grass is green, condensed in mist,
The pair of swallows fly, fluttering and twisting.
The Luo River flows, a single vein of blue,
People on the path are envied by all. <gloss>The first half of the poem describes the swallows and the view from afar.</gloss>

Deep within the emerald clouds is the hall where I once lived. <gloss>His eyes are fixed on his former palace, but he cannot fly there; he is truly inferior to the swallows who can return to their old nests. How tragic.</gloss>
Who will uphold loyalty and righteousness,
To vent the resentment within my heart? <gloss>The second half is his personal lament. The poetry is fine.</gloss>

Dong Zhuo frequently sent people to spy on them. On this day, they obtained this poem and presented it to him. Zhuo said, "Complaining and writing poetry gives me a justification to kill him." <gloss>To kill him with a stated reason is also a way to instruct the world.</gloss> He then ordered Li Ru to take eighteen warriors into the palace to assassinate the Emperor. The Emperor, the Empress Dowager, and the Consort were upstairs when a palace maid reported that Li Ru had arrived. The Emperor was greatly alarmed. Ru offered the Emperor <term>zhenjiu</term> <gloss>poisoned wine</gloss>. <gloss>Since the poem mentioned wine, this drink is a most elegant response.</gloss>

<summary>Dong Zhuo forces the scholar Cai Yong into service and discovers a poem written by the deposed Emperor Shao Di expressing grief. Using the poem as a pretext for treason, Zhuo sends Li Ru to the palace to execute the imperial family with poisoned wine.</summary>
<keywords>Dong Zhuo, Li Ru, Cai Yong, Shao Di, Empress Dowager He, Consort Tang, assassination, poisoned wine, poetry, Romance of the Three Kingdoms</keywords>
